 B) FURTHER DIRECTION MAY KINDLY BE ISSUED TO THE RESPONDENT NO.1 TO 4, NOT TO DEMOLISH THE REMAINING PORTION OF THE HOUSE BELONGING TO THE PETITIONER,
EXISTING IN THE SCHEDULE PROPERTY, AND ALSO NOT TO DISPOSSESS THE PETITIONER FROM THE SCHEDULE PROPERTY,
UNLESS THEY ACQUIRED THE LAND AND PAY THE COMPENSATION IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW AND ETC.

 ORDER

Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel appearing for respondents No.1 to 3/NHAI and learned HCGP appearing for respondent No.4/State as well as learned counsel appearing for respondent No.5/Union of India.

This petition is filed by the petitioner for mandamus seeking a direction to respondent No.3 to consider the representations date 25.06.2016, 27.09.2017 and 02.03.20218 and to the 2nd respondent to consider the representation dated 12.06.2018.

3. Petitioner submits that he along with his brother are the absolute owners and enjoyment of the property bearing Sy.No.21 of Math village in Kumata taluka, Uttara kannada District and they each have half share of their respective portion of the property.
Their names are also entered in the record of rights.
The house and commercial building of petitioner is situated in the said property bearing Panchayath Nos.33A, 33B and 33C.
It is also stated by the petitioner that there is a RCC roofed 19 year old building in existence in the said property.
The Chartered Engineer, who was visited the building has given report as plinth some area with RCC roofed building and some area of AC sheet roofed.
There is also an open well as well as bore well which is compounded with a compound wall.

The Ministry of Road Transport and Highway issued a notification under Section 3A(1) of the NC: 2024:KHC-D:7728 National Highways Act, 1956 (for short, 'the Act, 1956') for maintenance and operation of National Highway No.66 formerly called as NH-17.
4.

entities.text: Ministry of Road Transport and Highway
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The land of the petitioner bearing Sy.No.21 to an extent of 404 square meters was proposed to be acquired.

By the notification issued under Section 3(5)(a) of the Act, 1956, the total extent of land required for widening of the National Highway Project in Sy.No.21 of Math village of Kumata taluka is 267.2 square meters.
The land of petitioner partially has been acquired in Sy.No.21, but it is stated that the authorities have shown to acquire an extent of land of 404 square meters.
Petitioner admits that certain extent of land has been taken possession by the authorities and have also been demolished the portion of building belonging to petitioner.
The total extent of entire land is 13 guntas 10 annas and what has been proposed for acquisition is only 4 guntas.
The possession of said land has been taken by the National Highway Authorities.

They have calculated the compensation insofar as entire building in question, but they have not included the certain portions which are in the rear NC: 2024:KHC-D:7728 portion while calculating the building value for the purpose of compensation.

Hence, the respondent-authorities have committed a mistake in calculating the area proposed land is acquired and they have wrongly shown the property as Sy.No.20 as also land to be acquired by showing that the same would come within Sy.No.21.

It is also admitted by the petitioner that some portion in that front portion of the building and the vacant land in front of the building in the Sy.No.21 has already been demolished by the authorities, but the remaining portion has not been acquired and demolished.

sentences.text: It is the contention of learned counsel for the petitioner that there is a residential building which the respondent authorities are intending to acquire and demolish, but the same is un-acquired portion of the land.
Hence, it is illegal, arbitrary to demolish or occupy the un- acquired portion of land.
Hence, he filed a representation to the authorities to consider the same not to demolish or acquire the un-acquired portion of land, where the residential building is situated.

Learned counsel for respondents No.1 and 2 filed statement of objections and it is categorically stated, so also by the learned counsel representing the other respondents that they have no intention to demolish the remaining portion of the building, which is not acquired and hence the writ petition itself is not maintainable as there is no intention of respondents acquiring any further property of the petitioner.

The property that was sought to acquire was to maintain and manage the National Highways and accordingly, they have only acquired those portions as acquired in accordance with law and no compensation is payable for so called AC sheet roofed building to the extent of 35.71 square meters situated at rear portion of the building as it does not fall within the extent of land acquired or sought to be acquired.
Therefore, the remaining part of the building which is partially demolished will not be demolished by the respondent-authorities.

No attempt is also made by the respondents to demolish the AC sheet roofed building and in case the respondents intend to acquire in future, same will be done in accordance with law and NC: 2024:KHC-D:7728 compensation would be paid to the petitioner as per law.

It is categorically further stated by the learned counsel for respondents that there is no action taken for demolition of remaining portion of the building as presently there is no proposal to acquire the same.
The compensation amount whatever has been valued by the approved valuer, necessary amount would be paid by the respondent-authorities in case of any supplementary award.

7. Learned counsel for respondents would contend that the present petition is not maintainable in law, as there is an alternative efficacious remedy available with regard to inadequacy of compensation as per Section 3G(5) of the Act, 1956.

Under the circumstances, he contends that in case the petitioner is aggrieved by the inadequacy of compensation or lesser compensation, there is an alternative efficacious remedy, which can be explored by the petitioner.

8. With regard to prayer-b of the petition, not to demolish the remaining portion of the house belonging to the petitioner and neither dispossess the petitioner from the schedule property without proper acquisition of land or NC: 2024:KHC-D:7728 payment of compensation.

Learned counsel for the respondents has admitted that there is no direction for demolishing the remaining portion of the property and also they are not interested in dispossessing or demolishing remaining portion of the property, which has not been acquired by respondents by way of acquisition process.
In view of such categorical statement stated on oath by the respondents and so also submission by the learned counsel for other respondents, this petition could be disposed of.

Accordingly, I pass the following :
ORDER (i) Petition is disposed of.
Nagaraj
